page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single AMD EPYC physical core clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of memory, reflecting a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Performance profiles demonstrate marked contrast between single-threaded efficiency and aggregate multi-core throughput. In single-core benchmarks, the AMD EPYC core achieves top-tier results in stress-ng and strong ratings in Geekbench single-core, alongside fast gzip compression and bzip3 decompression throughput. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU and multi-core Geekbench reflect weak relative positioning, bounded by the physical limit of two hardware threads on a single core. Memory subsystem evaluations show average throughput, registering 70.08 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 63.38 GB/sec for writes.

Dedicated CPU allocation eliminates the noisy-neighbor interference characteristic of burstable infrastructure, delivering deterministic single-thread throughput. Given the modest memory footprint and bounded compute capacity, the voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is best fitted for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch scripts, monitoring agents, and CI/CD utility workloads requiring reliable per-core baseline performance without excessive RAM overhead.

This configuration provides a stable, dedicated execution profile suited for lightweight batch processing, single-threaded compute tasks, microservices, and small background automation workers requiring consistent per-core execution.
